for.label: Who it's for
for.definition: Who the resource speaks to: the person meant to read, watch or act. The same tree names who carries the message (messenger).

about.label: Who it's about
about.definition: Whose health it is about. Only groups the resource names.

stage.label: Where they are with it
stage.definition: Where the audience is with the behavior, from not started to in recovery.

concepts.label: The public, for themselves
concepts.definition: People reading or acting about their own health. The default for a campaign aimed at everyone.

concepts.label: Family and friends
concepts.definition: People who act for someone close to them.

concepts.label: Parents and caregivers
concepts.definition: Parents, guardians, grandparents and carers acting for a child or an adult they look after.

concepts.label: Partners and family members
concepts.definition: Spouses, partners, siblings and other relatives.

concepts.label: Friends and peers
concepts.definition: Friends, roommates, classmates, teammates, bystanders.

concepts.label: Health and care workers
concepts.definition: People who treat or care for patients.

concepts.label: Doctors
concepts.definition: Physicians of any specialty.

concepts.label: Primary care doctors and pediatricians
concepts.definition: Family doctors, GPs, internists, pediatricians.

concepts.label: Care home and home care staff
concepts.definition: Nursing assistants, personal care and aged-care workers.

concepts.label: Allied health professionals
concepts.definition: Therapists, technologists and technicians: physical, occupational, respiratory and speech therapy, imaging, dietitians, medical assistants. Added for TRAIN (2026-10-29).

concepts.label: Laboratory staff
concepts.definition: Clinical and public health laboratory scientists and technicians. Added for TRAIN (2026-10-29).

concepts.label: Addiction counselors
concepts.definition: SOC 2018 21-1018; O*NET splits it into 21-1011.00 (substance abuse and behavioral disorder) and 21-1014.00 (mental health).

concepts.label: Peer recovery and harm-reduction workers
concepts.definition: People with lived experience paid to support others, and harm-reduction outreach staff.

concepts.label: Hospital and clinic leaders
concepts.definition: Managers who set policy for a health system, hospital or clinic.

concepts.label: Public health workers
concepts.definition: Staff of health departments and prevention programs.

concepts.label: Community health workers
concepts.definition: Promotores, lay health workers, CHWs.

concepts.label: Environmental health staff
concepts.definition: Sanitarians, food, water, housing and lead inspectors. Added for TRAIN (2026-10-29).

concepts.label: Emergency management and preparedness staff
concepts.definition: Emergency managers and preparedness coordinators in health departments, hospitals and government. Added for TRAIN (2026-10-29).

concepts.label: Health departments and program managers
concepts.definition: The health department as an organization, and the managers who run its programs.

concepts.label: School and campus leaders
concepts.definition: Principals, superintendents, deans, residence life.

concepts.label: Celebrities, athletes and public figures
concepts.definition: Mainly a messenger value: famous people who front a campaign.

concepts.label: Other trusted messengers
concepts.definition: Elders, neighborhood leaders, people with lived experience speaking publicly.

concepts.label: Teens (13-17)
concepts.definition: MeSH Adolescent runs 13-18; campaigns for 18-year-olds go in Young adults.

concepts.label: Adults (25-64)
concepts.definition: Only when the campaign names an adult age range, not as a stand-in for everyone.

concepts.label: Older adults (65+)
concepts.definition: Campaigns saying 60+ or 55+ land here too.

concepts.label: Men who have sex with men
concepts.definition: A behavior, not an identity; used by HIV and STI campaigns.

concepts.label: White
concepts.definition: Rarely named; only when a campaign says so.

concepts.label: Indigenous peoples
concepts.definition: Works across countries.

concepts.label: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples

concepts.definition: Family, friends and people who have lost someone.

aclm-lmwphi-v4.title: ACLM Lifestyle Medicine Whole Person Health Index, version 4
aclm-lmwphi-v4.about: The patient-completed lifestyle assessment in ACLM's Epic Foundation build (Nova release note 923516, May 2026) and in eClinicalWorks 12.0.4 (Nov 2026): readiness, three priorities, the ACLM Diet Screener 9 v2, sleep, the Exercise Vital Sign plus strength, the PHQ-2 plus two stress items, meaning and connectedness, and five substance-use items. Section scores (score-*) follow ACLM's LMWPHI v4 administrator guide. Labels here are short paraphrases, not ACLM's wording.
aclm-lmwphi-v4.copyright: Instrument and scoring (c) 2026 American College of Lifestyle Medicine. PHQ-2 items: no permission required to reproduce. Item labels are paraphrased; use ACLM's form for the questions as asked. Which answers point to which HCF Audiences values is Health Culture Foundation's (CC BY 4.0) and unreviewed.

Readiness and confidence, total (0-20)
